title: March 2009 Class Hospital Final Supplementary Exam (Paper 1)
unit: Paper 1: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Anatomy and Physiology, Mental Health, Midwifery

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the March 2009 class Hospital Final Supplementary Examination Paper 1 (TNH, sat 14 November 2011, Part A, Q1 to Q20).

questions.text: After liver biopsy, the client is placed in the following position:
questions.explanation: Right-lateral (D) is correct because the liver lies under the right costal margin, so lying on the right side compresses the biopsy site against the chest wall, which reduces bleeding and bile leakage; the client stays in this position for 2 to 3 hours with vital signs monitored. Semi-fowlers (A) is incorrect because it does not apply pressure to the puncture site. Supine (B) is incorrect because it gives no compression of the site. Prone (C) is incorrect because it is uncomfortable and not used after the procedure.

questions.text: Exercise tolerance test is indicated in the following conditions:

options.C: Evaluation of chest pain, post myocardial infarction treatment

questions.explanation: Evaluation of chest pain, post myocardial infarction treatment (C) is correct because the stress (exercise tolerance) test is used to find out the presence of coronary artery disease in a patient with chest pain and to assess the functional capacity and the response to treatment after a myocardial infarction. Obvious heart failure, pericarditis (A), fever, acute myocarditis (B) and arrhythmias, uncontrolled hypertension (D) are incorrect because they are contraindications, as the stress of exercise could be dangerous.

questions.text: Patients with left sided heart failure may present with:
questions.explanation: Breathlessness, frothy white sputum (B) is correct because the failing left ventricle causes blood to back up into the lungs (pulmonary congestion), which gives dyspnoea, orthopnoea, cough and frothy (often pink-tinged) sputum. Ankle oedema, abdominal discomfort (A) and cyanosis, ascites (C) are incorrect because they are features of right sided failure (systemic venous congestion). Low pulse pressure, peripheral cyanosis (D) is incorrect because it describes low output or shock and is not the typical presentation.

questions.text: The appropriate diuretic for a client with cerebral oedema is:
questions.explanation: Mannitol (B) is correct because it is an osmotic diuretic that raises the plasma osmolality and draws water out of the brain tissue, which lowers the intracranial pressure. Furosemide (A) is a loop diuretic that may be used as an adjunct, but it is not the diuretic of choice. Hydrochlorothiazide (C) and spironolactone (D) are incorrect because they are used for hypertension and oedema of heart, liver and kidney disease and act too slowly to reduce raised ICP.

questions.text: Manifestations of severe airway obstruction include:

options.B: Wheezing, use of accessory muscles, Apnea
options.D: Cyanosis, inability to speak, ineffective cough

questions.explanation: Cyanosis, inability to speak, ineffective cough (D) is correct because in severe (complete) obstruction no air passes, so the patient cannot speak or cough effectively and becomes cyanosed, and may clutch the throat. Forceful cough, dyspnea, tachypnea (A) is incorrect because a forceful cough shows a mild obstruction. Wheezing, use of accessory muscles, apnea (B) is incorrect because it describes partial obstruction such as asthma. Bradypnea, crackles, asymmetrical chest movement (C) is incorrect because it points to lung or pleural problems and not to upper airway obstruction.

questions.text: The nurse will observe the following indicators while assessing patient's respiratory status:

options.A: Temperature of extremities, colour of fingers
options.B: Colour of palmar surfaces, respiratory rate
options.C: Oxygen saturation, sensation of the extremities
options.D: Colour of the extremities, nasal flaring

questions.explanation: Colour of the extremities, nasal flaring (D) is correct because cyanosis of the extremities shows poor oxygenation, and nasal flaring is a sign of respiratory distress. Temperature of extremities, colour of fingers (A) is incorrect because the temperature is a circulation indicator. Colour of palmar surfaces, respiratory rate (B) is partly correct because the respiratory rate is an important indicator, but the palmar surface colour is not a standard respiratory indicator. Oxygen saturation, sensation of the extremities (C) is incorrect because sensation is a neurological finding. Note: option B is also arguable, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: The physiological changes in the skin during aging include:

options.B: Skin becomes brittle, loss of hair
options.D: Dryness of skin, loss of sensation

questions.explanation: Dryness of skin, loss of sensation (D) is correct because with ageing the sebaceous and sweat gland activity falls, so the skin becomes dry, and the number of sensory receptors and nerve endings falls, so touch, pain and temperature sensation are reduced. Development of lesions, skin discoloration (A) is incorrect because lesions are mostly pathological or the result of sun damage. Skin becomes brittle, loss of hair (B) is incorrect because the skin becomes thin and less elastic, and the brittle change applies more to the nails. Wrinkling, exfoliation (C) is incorrect because exfoliation is not a typical physiological change of age. Note: wrinkling and hair loss are also age changes, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Cancer of the colon commonly occurs in the following region:
questions.explanation: Sigmoid colon (B) is correct because the rectosigmoid region is the commonest site of colorectal cancer (about 50% of cases). Ascending colon (A), transverse colon (C) and descending colon (D) are incorrect because they are less common sites.

questions.text: Ms. Jane had to quit her job to be a full time mother. This indicates that Ms. Jane is experiencing role:
questions.explanation: Conflict (B) is correct because role conflict occurs when the expectations of two roles (employee and mother) are incompatible, so that the person cannot fulfil both and has to give up one. Strain (A) is incorrect because it means difficulty in meeting the demands of a single role. Multiplicity (C) is incorrect because it means holding many roles at the same time, which does not by itself force the person to leave one. Reciprocal (D) is incorrect because it describes the complementary relationship between roles such as nurse and patient. Note: role strain is also arguable, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Before a bone marrow biopsy is done the nurse should enquire from the patient if they:

options.A: Have a family history of cancer

questions.explanation: Are on anticoagulants (B) is correct because the biopsy is an invasive procedure through the bone and carries a risk of bleeding, so the nurse must know whether the patient is on anticoagulants or has a bleeding disorder, and the platelet count and clotting are checked. A family history of cancer (A), a history of fracture (C) and persistent bone pain (D) are incorrect because they do not affect the safety of the procedure.

questions.text: A complication of hyperviscosity of polycythemia vera is:
questions.explanation: Thrombosis (D) is correct because the thickened blood from the high red cell mass flows sluggishly and clots in arteries and veins (stroke, myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis). Cardiomyopathy (A), pulmonary oedema (B) and DIC (C) are incorrect because they are not the direct result of hyperviscosity in polycythemia vera.

questions.text: The vector that transmits Rift Valley Fever is:
questions.explanation: Culex pipiens (A) is correct because Rift Valley fever virus is transmitted by mosquitoes, mainly Aedes (for example Aedes mcintoshi) and Culex species, including Culex pipiens, and of the options this is the genuine RVF vector. Aedes culex (B) is incorrect because it is not a recognised species. Aedes africanus (C) is incorrect because it is a vector of yellow fever in Africa. Aedes polynesiensis (D) is incorrect because it is a vector of lymphatic filariasis in the Pacific. Note: Aedes species are the main RVF vectors during outbreaks, but none of those is listed correctly.

questions.text: Mary has a phobia of cats on her first visit to her therapist. The therapist drops a cat on her. She screams until she accepts the cat is not harmful. This form of therapy is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Flooding (C) is correct because it is a behaviour therapy in which the patient is exposed suddenly and intensely to the feared object until the anxiety goes down and the patient learns it is harmless. Systematic desensitization (A) is incorrect because the exposure is gradual and combined with relaxation. Biofeedback (B) is incorrect because it teaches control of physiological responses using feedback from instruments. Assertive training (D) is incorrect because it teaches the patient to express feelings and needs directly.

questions.text: The hormones that are directly responsible for increased trunkal obesity in Cushing syndrome are:
questions.explanation: Cortisol, Aldosterone (A) is correct because excess cortisol redistributes fat to the trunk, face (moon face) and the back of the neck (buffalo hump) and breaks down limb muscle, while aldosterone causes sodium and water retention that adds to the truncal bulk. Estrogen, calcitonin (B), cortisol, thyroxine (C) and aldosterone, growth hormone (D) are incorrect because the second hormone in each pair does not cause the trunkal obesity of Cushing syndrome. Note: cortisol is the main cause.

questions.text: When assessing the gag reflex, the cranial nerves assessed are:
questions.explanation: IX and X (B) is correct because the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) carries the sensory part of the gag reflex from the pharynx, and the vagus nerve (X) carries the motor part, which contracts the pharyngeal muscles. X and XI (A), IX and XII (C) and VII and IX (D) are incorrect because XI, XII and VII are not part of the gag reflex arc.

questions.text: A premature is defined as:

options.A: A baby born before 28 weeks gestation
options.B: A baby born after 28 week but before 37 weeks gestation
options.C: A baby born between 28 weeks and 40 weeks of gestation
options.D: A baby born before 40 weeks of gestation

questions.explanation: A baby born after 28 weeks but before 37 weeks gestation (B) is correct because in midwifery in Kenya a premature (preterm) baby is one born after the age of viability (28 weeks) and before 37 completed weeks. A baby born before 28 weeks (A) is incorrect because it is an extremely preterm baby or an abortion (miscarriage), depending on viability. A baby born between 28 and 40 weeks (C) and before 40 weeks (D) are incorrect because they include term babies (37 to 42 weeks).

questions.text: Daily examination of normal baby includes checking for:

options.B: Discharge from the eyes, head circumference, chest expansion
options.D: State of the umbilical cord, skin colour, chest expansion

questions.explanation: Jaundice, oral thrush, weight (A) is correct because the daily routine check of a normal newborn includes the skin (jaundice), the mouth (thrush), the weight, the cord, the eyes, the passage of urine and stool, and feeding. Head circumference (B) is incorrect because it is measured at birth and later at intervals. Moulding (C) is incorrect because it is assessed in the first days. State of the umbilical cord, skin colour, chest expansion (D) is partly correct (the cord and skin are checked daily), but chest expansion is not a routine daily check. Note: option D is also arguable, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Before administering pethidine during labour, the midwife should:

options.D: Determine the descent of presenting part

questions.explanation: Establish the cervical dilation (A) is correct because pethidine is given only when the labour is established (cervix about 4 cm or more) and not when delivery is expected within about 2 to 4 hours, as the drug crosses the placenta and can cause respiratory depression in the newborn. Determining the foetal heart rate (B) is also done but it is a general assessment. Assessing contractions (C) and the descent of the presenting part (D) are incorrect because they are not the key deciding factor. Note: the fetal heart rate is also checked before and after the injection.

questions.text: The management of engorged breasts includes:

options.A: Administering analgesics, expressing breast milk, applying warm compresses
options.B: Administering antibiotics, expressing breast milk, putting the baby off the breast
options.C: Suppressing lactation, administering analgesics, applying cold compresses
options.D: Supporting the breasts, administering antibiotics, putting the baby on the breast

questions.explanation: Administering analgesics, expressing breast milk, applying warm compresses (A) is correct because engorgement is treated by relieving the pain, removing the milk (expressing and frequent feeding) and applying warmth to help the milk flow. Antibiotics (B, D) are incorrect because engorgement is not an infection, and putting the baby off the breast (B) leaves the milk stagnant. Suppressing lactation and cold compresses (C) are incorrect because breastfeeding is encouraged.

questions.text: The cardinal signs of pre-eclampsia include:
questions.explanation: Proteinuria, high blood pressure, oedema (B) is correct because the classic triad of pre-eclampsia is hypertension, proteinuria and oedema. High blood pressure, dizziness, oedema (A) is incorrect because dizziness is a symptom and proteinuria is missing. Glycosuria, proteinuria, epigastric pain (C) is incorrect because glycosuria is not a sign, and epigastric pain is a sign of severe disease. Vomiting, frontal headache, convulsions (D) are incorrect because they are impending signs of eclampsia.
